handoff.goals: Install the PostHog React Native SDK using the project's package manager, including required peer/configuration libraries.
handoff.did: Installed `posthog-react-native`, its required `react-native-svg` peer dependency, and `react-native-config` with the detected npm package manager. The resolved published versions are declared in `package.json` and locked in `package-lock.json`; later integration steps should import from `posthog-react-native` and load build-time configuration through `react-native-config`.
handoff.forNextAgent: Use `posthog-react-native` for client instrumentation and `react-native-config` for `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `POSTHOG_HOST`. This Expo project now has native dependencies that may require a development build/prebuild rather than Expo Go for runtime validation.
handoff.evidence: Ran `npm add posthog-react-native react-native-svg react-native-config` successfully. npm reported 17 packages added; manifest contains `posthog-react-native` `^4.63.0`, `react-native-config` `^1.6.1`, and `react-native-svg` `^15.15.5`; corresponding root dependency entries appear in `package-lock.json`.
handoff.assumptions: No server-side event-sending code was evaluated because this task was limited to installing the React Native client SDK and explicitly required peers/configuration library. The npm peer-resolution output was warnings for existing Clerk/React version constraints and did not prevent installation.
handoff.conflict: None; installation completed despite non-fatal existing Clerk/React peer-dependency warnings.

handoff.goals: Initialize PostHog once for the Expo React Native app, configure its environment variables, and document those variables for developers.
handoff.did: Created `lib/posthog.ts`, which constructs the singleton `posthog` client from `EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST`. It captures app lifecycle events and enables SDK debug logging in development. If either setting is missing, development logs the prescribed clear configuration error; production leaves `posthog` null so app startup remains a no-op. Updated `app/_layout.tsx` to mount `PostHogProvider` around the Expo Router stack only when the singleton is configured, making `usePostHog()` the downstream call-site access pattern. Wrote the real public token and host to `.env` through `set_env_values`, and created `.env.example` with non-production placeholder/documentation values. This establishes the shared PostHog client for all future identification, capture, and error-tracking work.
handoff.forNextAgent: Import `usePostHog` from `posthog-react-native` in components nested under the root layout; it reaches the singleton provided by `PostHogProvider`. For module-level/non-React work, import `{ posthog }` from `@/lib/posthog` and guard for null. Do not construct a second client. The app uses Expo Router rather than a manually declared NavigationContainer. No web Content-Security-Policy was found or changed. The SDK dependencies (`posthog-react-native`, `react-native-svg`, and `react-native-config`) were already added to `package.json` by the concurrent install task; this task did not install packages or run builds/tests as instructed.
handoff.evidence: `check_env_keys` verified both `EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `EXPO_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` are present in `.env`. Final reads verified the client module and root-provider wiring. `package.json` showed `posthog-react-native` and `react-native-svg` installed. No builds, linters, or tests were run per task instructions.
handoff.assumptions: Expo public environment variables are embedded at build time and are the codebase's existing environment convention, evidenced by `EXPO_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` in the root layout. Since this is an Expo app, the Expo environment convention was used instead of bare React Native's `react-native-config` access pattern.

handoff.goals: Identify authenticated client users with a stable identifier at completed login/sign-up and reset PostHog identity after logout.
handoff.did: Updated `app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx` to identify with Clerk `session.userId` after successful password and MFA/client-trust sign-in completion, while writing email only to the `$set` person property. Updated `app/(auth)/sign-up.tsx` to identify newly verified users with the same stable Clerk ID and email person property. Updated `app/(tabs)/settings.tsx` to call `posthog.reset()` only after Clerk sign-out succeeds. This lets all later client captures and SDK-reported errors inherit the persistent Clerk identity, and prevents identity leakage between users after logout.
handoff.forNextAgent: This is a client-only Expo app. Do not identify again in ordinary event/error call sites: use the shared initialized client (`usePostHog()` within the root provider or guarded `posthog` from `@/lib/posthog`) and it will inherit the persisted distinct ID. Do not place email, names, or other PII in event properties.
handoff.evidence: Final source reads verified the three guarded `posthog?.identify(session.userId, { $set: { email } })` calls in completed Clerk auth paths and `posthog?.reset()` after successful sign-out. No builds, linters, or tests were run because this task explicitly prohibited them.
handoff.assumptions: Clerk's finalized session exposes `userId`, as used by the app's authenticated Clerk session flow; calls are guarded so no undefined distinct ID is passed. Email is available from the completed auth form and is used only as a person property.

handoff.goals: Configure one global React Native/Expo error-capture mechanism so otherwise uncaught rendering errors reach PostHog.
handoff.did: Edited app/_layout.tsx to mount the SDK-provided PostHogErrorBoundary inside the existing conditional PostHogProvider and around the Expo Router Stack. Added a minimal RootErrorFallback UI. This captures root-level React rendering exceptions as PostHog error-tracking exceptions through the SDK rather than manual capture calls. It feeds the PostHog Error Tracking exception stream for uncaught render failures.
handoff.forNextAgent: The error boundary is conditional with the already-configured posthog singleton, preserving the existing no-op behavior when configuration is absent. No other error handlers or per-route wrappers were added. Later review/build work should validate compilation and runtime delivery.
handoff.evidence: Read the task guidance, React Native SDK reference, and final app/_layout.tsx. The final source shows PostHogErrorBoundary wrapping the router Stack within PostHogProvider.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed posthog-react-native ^4.63.0 exports PostHogErrorBoundary as documented by the supplied React Native reference. No build or tests were run, as explicitly required.

handoff.goals: Select meaningful React Native user actions, instrument them with PostHog capture calls, and record the resulting event contract.
handoff.did: Created `.posthog-wizard-cache/.posthog-events.json` with five event definitions. Added guarded custom captures for completed password/client-trust sign-in (`user_signed_in`), completed verified sign-up (`user_signed_up`), successful sign-out before identity reset (`user_signed_out`), subscription detail expansion/collapse (`subscription_details_toggled`), and daily verse bookmark toggling (`daily_verse_bookmark_toggled`). Authentication captures run after the existing Clerk identification call; no PII is included in event properties.
handoff.forNextAgent: All custom events use the initialized guarded `posthog` singleton and are attributed through the persisted Clerk identity. `app/(tabs)/index2.tsx` is an additional Expo route with the bookmark interaction; the configured tabs list uses `index.tsx` as Home. No tests/builds/linters were run because this capture task expressly prohibits them.
handoff.evidence: Final reads confirmed five planned-event records and `capture()` calls placed in successful Clerk finalization, successful sign-out before reset, and the two in-app press handlers. No PII is passed as an event property.
handoff.assumptions: The existing Clerk identify calls persist identity before capture as established by the identify-task handoff; the shared client is configured via the root provider and optional singleton export.

handoff.goals: Create a starter PostHog dashboard containing meaningful insights based on the events instrumented by the React Native integration.
handoff.did: Created the PostHog dashboard `Analytics basics (wizard)` (ID 1995733), tagged `wizard`, with its required description. Created and attached five wizard-tagged insights: `Signup to sign-in funnel (wizard)` using `user_signed_up` → `user_signed_in`; `New user signups (wizard)` using `user_signed_up`; `Completed sign-ins (wizard)` using `user_signed_in`; `Subscription detail engagement (wizard)` using `subscription_details_toggled`; and `Daily verse bookmarks (wizard)` using `daily_verse_bookmark_toggled`. These supply acquisition, authentication, conversion, and feature-engagement dashboard views.
handoff.forNextAgent: Dashboard URL: https://us.posthog.com/project/258299/dashboard/1995733. All insights are intentionally defined even if no events have arrived yet; they will populate when the newly instrumented events are captured.
handoff.evidence: PostHog MCP returned dashboard ID 1995733 and URL https://us.posthog.com/project/258299/dashboard/1995733. It also returned successful saved insight responses with dashboard tile associations for insight IDs 11027372, 11027373, 11027376, 11027375, and 11027374.
handoff.assumptions: The five event names and their intended semantics were taken directly from the upstream capture-task handoff, as instructed.
